These are well-established/recitable. The candidate adds four additional composite terms: (a) G/(N^alpha·V^beta) — a model-capacity/vocabulary interaction; (b) H/(V^delta·D^gamma·(1+kappa·log V)^eta) — a vocabulary/data-efficiency interaction modulated by a logarithmic tokenizer-compression saturation factor; (c) J/(N^alpha·D^gamma·(1+kappa·log V)^mu) — a capacity-data joint term modulated by the same compression saturation factor; (d) K/(N^alpha·V^beta·D^gamma·(1+kappa·log V)^nu) — a triple capacity-vocabulary-data joint utilization term also modulated by the log-compression factor. Step 2 — Recitability: The individual power-law form is textbook-standard, but the full combined structure is not. In particular, the recurring saturation modulator (1+kappa·log V)^{eta/mu/nu} applied multiplicatively to interaction denominators is a nontrivial, non-standard construction. No existing textbook or public scaling-law reference (Kaplan, Chinchilla/Hoffmann, Tao et al. vocabulary scaling) contains this exact multi-term composite form with logarithmic tokenizer-compression saturation embedded into pairwise and triple joint-utilization terms. An LLM could recite the baseline four terms and possibly guess a simple G/(N^alpha·V^beta) cross term, but the specific H, J, K terms with the shared log-based saturation exponents are not guessable from background knowledge alone.
